blocks.prompt: 5 (i) Solve the following system by reducing its augmented matrix to the echelon form and the reduced echelon form: \(x_1 + 2x_2 - 2x_3 = -1\), \(2x_1 + 3x_2 + x_3 = 1\), \(5x_1 + 4x_2 - 3x_3 = 1\)
blocks.explanation:
A non-homogeneous system of three equations, solved with row operations on \([A \mid B]\).
We must find the three unknowns, using both forms.
Plan: echelon form and back substitution; continue to reduced echelon form and read the answer; check.
steps:
Given: \(x_1 + 2x_2 - 2x_3 = -1\), \(2x_1 + 3x_2 + x_3 = 1\), \(5x_1 + 4x_2 - 3x_3 = 1\)
To find: \(x_1, x_2, x_3\) by reducing the augmented matrix to echelon form and to reduced echelon form.
Method: Write the augmented matrix \([A \mid B]\). Row operations change the equations into equivalent ones (same solution). Echelon form: leading 1s with zeros below, then back substitution. Reduced echelon form: also zeros above the leading 1s, then the answer can be read directly.

Augmented matrix
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4 & -3 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Each row is one equation: coefficients on the left of the bar, the constant on the right.

Leading 1 in row 2
By \((-1)R_2 \to R_2'\)
\(R_2'\): \(0\), \(1\), \(-5\) | \(-3\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & -6 & 7 & 6\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Multiplying \(R_2\) by \(-1\) turns \(-1\) into 1.

Leading 1 in row 3
By \(\left(-\frac{1}{23}\right)R_3 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0\), \(0\), \(1\) | \(\frac{12}{23}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{12}{23}\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Dividing \(R_3\) by \(-23\). The matrix is now in (row) echelon form.

Back substitution from the echelon form
The echelon form stands for the system
\[x_1 + 2x_2 - 2x_3 = -1\]
\[x_2 - 5x_3 = -3\]
\[x_3 = \frac{12}{23}\]
Work upwards from the last equation:
\[x_3 = \dfrac{12}{23}\]
\[x_2 = -3 + 5\left(\frac{12}{23}\right)\]
\[x_2 = -\dfrac{9}{23}\]
\[x_1 = -1 - 2\left(-\frac{9}{23}\right) + 2\left(\frac{12}{23}\right)\]
\[x_1 = \dfrac{19}{23}\]
Why: The last row gives the third unknown at once; each row above then has only one new unknown.

Reduced form: clear column 2 above the pivot
By \(R_1 + (-2)R_2 \to R_1'\)
\(R_1'\): \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(2 - 2 = 0\), \(-2 + 10 = 8\) | \(-1 + 6 = 5\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 8 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{12}{23}\end{array}\right]\]
Why: \(2 + (-2)(1) = 0\). In reduced echelon form every pivot column has zeros above the pivot too.

Read the answer from the reduced echelon form
\[x_1 = \dfrac{19}{23}\]
\[x_2 = -\dfrac{9}{23}\]
\[x_3 = \dfrac{12}{23}\]
Why: Each row of the reduced form says (unknown) = (number). Both forms give the same answer.

Check in the original equations
\[\left(\frac{19}{23}\right) + 2\left(-\frac{9}{23}\right) - 2\left(\frac{12}{23}\right) = -1 \;\checkmark\]
\[2\left(\frac{19}{23}\right) + 3\left(-\frac{9}{23}\right) + \left(\frac{12}{23}\right) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
\[5\left(\frac{19}{23}\right) + 4\left(-\frac{9}{23}\right) - 3\left(\frac{12}{23}\right) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Always check in the original equations, not in the reduced ones.

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) Solve the following system by reducing its augmented matrix to the echelon form and the reduced echelon form: \(x + 2y + z = 2\), \(2x + y + 2z = 3\), \(2x + 3y - z = 7\)
blocks.explanation:
A non-homogeneous system of three equations, solved with row operations on \([A \mid B]\).
We must find the three unknowns, using both forms.
Plan: echelon form and back substitution; continue to reduced echelon form and read the answer; check.
steps:
Given: \(x + 2y + z = 2\), \(2x + y + 2z = 3\), \(2x + 3y - z = 7\)
To find: \(x, y, z\) by reducing the augmented matrix to echelon form and to reduced echelon form.
Method: Write the augmented matrix \([A \mid B]\). Row operations change the equations into equivalent ones (same solution). Echelon form: leading 1s with zeros below, then back substitution. Reduced echelon form: also zeros above the leading 1s, then the answer can be read directly.

Augmented matrix
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 & 7\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Each row is one equation: coefficients on the left of the bar, the constant on the right.

Leading 1 in row 2
By \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)R_2 \to R_2'\)
\(R_2'\): \(0\), \(1\), \(0\) | \(\frac{1}{3}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Dividing \(R_2\) by \(-3\).

Leading 1 in row 3
By \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)R_3 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0\), \(0\), \(1\) | \(-\frac{10}{9}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{10}{9}\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Dividing \(R_3\) by \(-3\): \(\frac{10}{3} \div (-3) = -\frac{10}{9}\). The matrix is now in echelon form.

Back substitution from the echelon form
The echelon form stands for the system
\[x + 2y + z = 2\]
\[y = \frac{1}{3}\]
\[z = -\frac{10}{9}\]
Work upwards from the last equation:
\[z = -\dfrac{10}{9}\]
\[y = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[x = 2 - 2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) - \left(-\frac{10}{9}\right)\]
\[x = \dfrac{22}{9}\]
Why: The last row gives the third unknown at once; each row above then has only one new unknown.

Clear column 3 above the pivot
By \(R_1 + (-1)R_3 \to R_1'\)
\(R_1'\): \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(1 - 1 = 0\) | \(\frac{4}{3} + \frac{10}{9} = \frac{22}{9}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & \frac{22}{9} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{10}{9}\end{array}\right]\]
Why: \(1 + (-1)(1) = 0\); \(R_2\) already has 0 there. This is the reduced echelon form.

Read the answer from the reduced echelon form
\[x = \dfrac{22}{9}\]
\[y = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[z = -\dfrac{10}{9}\]
Why: Each row of the reduced form says (unknown) = (number). Both forms give the same answer.

Check in the original equations
\[\left(\frac{22}{9}\right) + 2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + \left(-\frac{10}{9}\right) = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[2\left(\frac{22}{9}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + 2\left(-\frac{10}{9}\right) = 3 \;\checkmark\]
\[2\left(\frac{22}{9}\right) + 3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) - \left(-\frac{10}{9}\right) = 7 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Always check in the original equations, not in the reduced ones.

blocks.prompt: 5 (iii) Solve the following system by reducing its augmented matrix to the echelon form and the reduced echelon form: \(x_1 + 4x_2 + x_3 = 2\), \(2x_1 + x_2 - 2x_3 = 9\), \(3x_1 + x_2 - x_3 = 12\)
blocks.explanation:
A non-homogeneous system of three equations, solved with row operations on \([A \mid B]\).
We must find the three unknowns, using both forms.
Plan: echelon form and back substitution; continue to reduced echelon form and read the answer; check.
steps:
Given: \(x_1 + 4x_2 + x_3 = 2\), \(2x_1 + x_2 - 2x_3 = 9\), \(3x_1 + x_2 - x_3 = 12\)
To find: \(x_1, x_2, x_3\) by reducing the augmented matrix to echelon form and to reduced echelon form.
Method: Write the augmented matrix \([A \mid B]\). Row operations change the equations into equivalent ones (same solution). Echelon form: leading 1s with zeros below, then back substitution. Reduced echelon form: also zeros above the leading 1s, then the answer can be read directly.

Augmented matrix
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 9 \\ 3 & 1 & -1 & 12\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Each row is one equation: coefficients on the left of the bar, the constant on the right.

Simplify row 3 before dividing
By \(R_3 + (-1)R_2 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(-11 + 7 = -4\), \(-4 + 4 = 0\) | \(6 - 5 = 1\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -7 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Why: \(-4 - (-4) = 0\) in column 3: row 3 becomes \((0, -4, 0 \mid 1)\), which avoids sevenths.

Put the simpler row second
By \(R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & -4 & 5\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Row \((0, -4, 0 \mid 1)\) gives a pivot with no other entries.

Leading 1 in row 2
By \(\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)R_2 \to R_2'\)
\(R_2'\): \(0\), \(1\), \(0\) | \(-\frac{1}{4}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & -7 & -4 & 5\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Dividing \(R_2\) by \(-4\).

Leading 1 in row 3
By \(\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)R_3 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0\), \(0\), \(1\) | \(-\frac{13}{16}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{13}{16}\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Dividing \(R_3\) by \(-4\). The matrix is now in echelon form.

Back substitution from the echelon form
The echelon form stands for the system
\[x_1 + 4x_2 + x_3 = 2\]
\[x_2 = -\frac{1}{4}\]
\[x_3 = -\frac{13}{16}\]
Work upwards from the last equation:
\[x_3 = -\dfrac{13}{16}\]
\[x_2 = -\dfrac{1}{4}\]
\[x_1 = 2 - 4\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) - \left(-\frac{13}{16}\right)\]
\[x_1 = \dfrac{61}{16}\]
Why: The last row gives the third unknown at once; each row above then has only one new unknown.

Clear column 3 above the pivot
By \(R_1 + (-1)R_3 \to R_1'\)
\(R_1'\): \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(1 - 1 = 0\) | \(3 + \frac{13}{16} = \frac{61}{16}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & \frac{61}{16} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{13}{16}\end{array}\right]\]
Why: \(1 + (-1)(1) = 0\); \(R_2\) already has 0 there. This is the reduced echelon form.

Read the answer from the reduced echelon form
\[x_1 = \dfrac{61}{16}\]
\[x_2 = -\dfrac{1}{4}\]
\[x_3 = -\dfrac{13}{16}\]
Why: Each row of the reduced form says (unknown) = (number). Both forms give the same answer.

Check in the original equations
\[\left(\frac{61}{16}\right) + 4\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) + \left(-\frac{13}{16}\right) = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[2\left(\frac{61}{16}\right) + \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) - 2\left(-\frac{13}{16}\right) = 9 \;\checkmark\]
\[3\left(\frac{61}{16}\right) + \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) - \left(-\frac{13}{16}\right) = 12 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Always check in the original equations, not in the reduced ones.
